module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 469

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/469](https://www.erdosproblems.com/469)
- [Le25] Lewis, Z. J., *On the convergence of the reciprocal sum of primitive pseudoperfect
  numbers*. Preprint (2025).
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos469

/-- The proposition that `n` is a sum of distinct proper divisors. -/
def Nat.IsSumDivisors (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ S ⊆ n.properDivisors, ∑ d ∈ S, d = n

open Erdos469

/--
Let $A$ be the set of all $n$ such that $n = d_1 + ⋯ + d_k$ with $d_i$ distinct
proper divisors of $n$, but this is not true for any $m ∣ n$ with $m < n$. Does:
$$
  \sum_{n ∈ A} \frac 1 n
$$
converge?

Yes: the sum converges. This was proved by Lewis [Le25], whose proof has been formalized in
Lean.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/68da20b96673899166e94638f5a7fffeb7231d35/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos469.lean"]
theorem erdos_469 :
    letI A := {n : ℕ | 0 < n ∧ n.IsSumDivisors ∧ ∀ m < n, m ∣ n → ¬ m.IsSumDivisors}
    answer(True) ↔ Summable fun n : A ↦ 1 / (n : ℝ) := by
  sorry

end Erdos469

findings.description: The module docstring cites the proof as "[Le25] Lewis, Z. J., *On the convergence of the reciprocal sum of primitive pseudoperfect numbers*. Preprint (2025)", and the `erdos_469` docstring points to it ("proved by Lewis [Le25]"). The only preprint the source links has a different title and year. It is "Convergence of the Reciprocal Sum of Primitive Semiperfect Numbers" by Zachary J. Lewis, dated July 2026. None of its version history is from 2025. This is a reference slip only; the mathematics is not affected.
findings.source_evidence: erdosproblems.com/469 (read via its LaTeX page) says "The convergence of this series was [proved](https://github.com/ZachL111/erdos469-preprint/blob/main/paper/output/pdf/erdos469_v1_2_1_preprint.pdf) by Lewis using GPT 5.6 and Claude Fable 5." In that repository, paper/main.tex has `\title{Convergence of the Reciprocal Sum of Primitive Semiperfect Numbers}` and `\date{Version 1.2.1, July 13, 2026}`. The README asks readers to cite "Zachary J. Lewis, *Convergence of the Reciprocal Sum of Primitive Semiperfect Numbers*, version 1.2.1 (2026)", and CITATION.cff gives year 2026. paper/CHANGELOG.md lists only v1.2 (2026-07-11) and v1.2.1 (2026-07-13). teorth/erdosproblems problems.yaml records 469 as proved with last_update 2026-07-21. The arXiv API returns no Lewis preprint on pseudoperfect or semiperfect numbers. The local git log shows the solved status and reference were added on 2026-08-04, after the July 2026 preprint.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the reference with "[Le26] Lewis, Z. J., *Convergence of the Reciprocal Sum of Primitive Semiperfect Numbers*. Preprint, v1.2.1 (2026). https://github.com/ZachL111/erdos469-preprint" and change "[Le25]" to "[Le26]" in the `erdos_469` docstring.

reformulations.difference: The source asks whether the series ∑_{n∈A} 1/n converges over positive integers. The Lean asks for `Summable fun n : A ↦ 1 / (n : ℝ)`: unconditional summability over the subtype of ℕ, with `0 < n` written into the set.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: All terms are nonnegative, so unconditional summability is the same as ordinary convergence of the partial sums. I proved this for every A ⊆ ℕ: `(Summable fun n : A ↦ 1/(n:ℝ)) ↔ ∃ L, Tendsto (fun N ↦ ∑ n ∈ (range N).filter (· ∈ A), 1/(n:ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 L)`. The proof uses `summable_subtype_iff_indicator`, `HasSum.tendsto_sum_nat` and `summable_iff_not_tendsto_nat_atTop_of_nonneg`. The `0 < n` condition leaves out 0, which would otherwise satisfy the predicate through the empty sum. Its term would be 1/0 = 0 anyway. In the minimality clause, m = 0 is excluded automatically, because 0 does not divide a positive n. So the Lean set is exactly the source's positive integers.

review.notes:
The main theorem states the source's problem faithfully. The source (erdosproblems.com/469) says: "Let A be the set of all n such that n = d_1+⋯+d_k with d_i distinct proper divisors of n, but this is not true for any m∣n with m<n. Does ∑_{n∈A} 1/n converge?" It identifies A with the primitive pseudoperfect numbers (OEIS A006036).

Checks on the Lean:
- With `pp.fullNames`, `n.IsSumDivisors` resolves to `Erdos469.Nat.IsSumDivisors`; there is no root-level `Nat.IsSumDivisors`.
- `Nat.properDivisors` includes 1, as A006036 requires (6 = 1+2+3).
- `IsSumDivisors 0` is true (empty sum) and `IsSumDivisors 1` is false; neither affects the set.
- I evaluated the file's set predicate verbatim: it gives [6, 20, 28, 88, 104] for n ≤ 120. A subset-sum DP, checked against the definition on n ≤ 120, gives 32 elements up to 2000, identical to the A006036 b-file. The pseudoperfect numbers up to 120 match A005835, with 70 (a weird number) excluded.
- `answer(True)` elaborates to `True ↔ Summable …`, which matches the source's "solved in the affirmative".

Status is consistent: the source shows "PROVED (LEAN)", and problems.yaml has "proved (Lean)" (2026-07-21). This matches `research solved`, `answer(True)` and `formal_proof using lean4`.

The linked plby file, at a pinned commit, proves exactly the file's right-hand side. It uses the same `letI A := …` and an identical `Nat.IsSumDivisors` body, so it implies `True ↔ …`. A grep of that file and of its `Util/Density.lean` import finds no `sorry`, `axiom`, `native_decide`, `opaque` or `implemented_by`. I did not compile the 20k-line proof, because it targets Lean/Mathlib v4.32.0 and this sandbox has v4.33.1.

The source's variant questions are not formalized in the file. These are the A119425 set, and the third Benkoski–Erdős set of n with a divisor that is a distinct sum of other divisors. Leaving them out is a coverage gap, not a misformalization.

I could not read Benkoski–Erdős 1974 directly (image-only scan). Its definition is corroborated by the source's own identification with A006036, by MathWorld (Guy 1994, p. 46), and by Lewis's preprint, which calls it the inclusive definition from [BeEr74, p. 617].
